per_shot.note: Molten serpent erupting into open cavern; self-glow hazes the dark around it and reads as a threat; segmented body gets busy at play size.
Head, mandibles and glowing seams read clearly; warm bloom lands in the air and beam haze, still in VEIL amber; head core blows out to white.
Small crystal spider on a lava shelf with the pod for scale; violet/cyan accent against amber works and lights the wall beside it, but it is tiny and the legs are thin at play size.
Faceted crystal crown plus white fangs sells 'ore that bites'; cool glow washes the rock face it clings to.
Two lit mannequin figures in the bright core chamber; they glow and light the floor, but against an amber-flooded room they barely separate and do not read as pursuers.
Clean faceted bodies with ember sparks; floor pools warm under them; posture is neutral and statue-like, no menace.
Ice-cyan flock with emissive points glowing in the lamp beam; sits in CRYOS palette; their own light barely reaches the rock below.
Faceted wings plus glowing cores read as living light; bloom is soft and on-palette; wing silhouettes slightly lost inside the glow.

top_issues.issue: Kindled have no threat and get lost in the bright core chamber
top_issues.why: A pursuer made of light reads as two calm white statues; the core room is already flooded with amber, so their light adds nothing and nothing about them says danger.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give them a forward-leaning, reaching pose and a hotter or contrasting core (white-gold with a darker shell, or a flicker), and darken their immediate surround so their own light pool is the brightest thing near them.

top_issues.issue: Rimewings' glow does not land on the world
top_issues.why: House style is 'lit by itself in the dark'; the flock is visible mainly because the headlamp beam is on it, and the rock below gets no cyan spill.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add a small shared cyan light that follows the flock centroid so the ice floor and walls pick up a moving cool wash, and keep them visible outside the beam.

top_issues.issue: Long One body becomes noisy at play size
top_issues.why: Many small bright segments merge into a jagged blob; the head-to-tail read weakens in the gameplay frame.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Fewer, chunkier segments with darker gaps between plates so the S-curve silhouette reads, and keep the brightest value at the head only.

top_issues.issue: Geode Mimic is small and spindly in the gameplay frame
top_issues.why: At play scale the thin legs vanish and it reads as a sparkle more than a biting creature.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Thicken legs and enlarge the jaw/fang wedge so the dangerous end reads at distance; keep the crystal crown as the ore disguise.

protect: Long One's molten amber self-glow and the warm haze it throws into the dark
Mimic's violet-crystal accent against VEIL amber, and its cool light washing the rock it sits on
Mimic's crystal crown plus white fangs reading as 'ore that bites'
Rimewings' emissive cores and ice-cyan palette
Faceted low-poly construction on all four

per_shot.note: Serpent laid flat like a plank across a pocket, with a lamp structure sitting directly under it; the two shapes overlap and the creature's silhouette and threat are muddled.
A bright hexagonal beacon sits in front of the serpent's body and steals the focal point; the body reads as stacked boards, head small; little of its own glow.
Mimic tiny on a dark cave wall beside a pink ore tile that competes with it; cool glow lands but the creature is hard to find.
Crystal spider under a ceiling ledge, cyan light washes the block above; mouth/fangs barely read, so it looks less dangerous than A.
Same staging as A; feet burn into a stronger white pool on the floor, more 'made of light' but legs dissolve; still no menace.
Lower bodies blow out into the floor glow; stronger light-lands than A but silhouette loses its legs; equal overall.
Pale shards visible only because the lamp hits them; no self-glow, so they read as paper birds rather than living light.
Wing shapes are crisper and more legible than A, but unlit by themselves; fails the house 'glow that lands' rule.

top_issues.issue: Long One staged on top of a lamp/beacon structure
top_issues.why: The beacon is brighter than the creature and overlaps its body, so the threat loses focal priority and the silhouette tangles.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Stage the serpent away from other light sources in dark rock so its own glow is the only light, as in A.

top_issues.issue: Long One reads as a flat rigid plank
top_issues.why: Straight horizontal body with uniform segments has no burrowing curve and low emissive, so it reads as debris.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Restore an S-curve and the molten seam emissive between plates; bring the head forward and brighten it.

top_issues.why: Without emissive cores they exist only inside the headlamp beam, which contradicts the creatures-as-light house style.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Bring back emissive cyan cores and add a light that spills onto the ice, while keeping B's crisper wing shapes.

top_issues.issue: Mimic hard to find at play size and competing with nearby ore
top_issues.why: Tiny violet shape on a black wall next to a saturated pink tile; the eye goes to the ore, not the creature.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Put it on a floor or ledge with pod-for-scale as in A, enlarge it, and keep competing emissive tiles out of its immediate surround.

top_issues.why: Same as A: calm statues in a room already full of amber light.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Aggressive pose plus darker local surround so their light is what you see.

protect: Kindled feet burning into the floor: a stronger light-lands pool than A
Mimic's cyan wash on the ceiling block in the close-up

why: A stages the Long One and Mimic as self-lit threats in the dark and keeps the Rimewings emissive; B buries the Long One behind a beacon and strips the Rimewings' glow. Kindled are effectively equal.
